candidates: When converting module-level functions to methods on a class (such as `ClassDB`), define them as regular class methods rather than arrow-function class properties. If a method needs a stable `this` binding for external callers (e.g., JISON parser callbacks), add a `.bind(this)` call in the constructor — do not rely on the arrow-function property form as a substitute.

In diagram DB classes that maintain a JISON-binding section in their constructor (as in `ClassDB`), only call `.bind(this)` for methods that are directly invoked by the JISON grammar. Private helper methods that are only called from other class methods internally do not need constructor bindings and should not be included in that section.

Private class methods that never reference `this` and have no dependency on instance state (e.g., pure lookup/mapping utilities like `getArrowMarker`) should be extracted as module-level functions outside the class body rather than kept as private class methods.
Enum-like constant objects exposed as class members (e.g., `lineType`, `relationType` in `ClassDB`) must be declared with the `readonly` modifier to prevent accidental mutation of their values.
